bull.thesis_summary: The stock is deeply oversold (RSI 26.62), the options market shows a near‑perfect put‑call parity (PCR 0.998), and the broader environment is low‑volatility (VIX 12.81, HV Rank 9.7/100). This combination suggests the pricing pressure that forced the market into the oversold region is likely to unwind, giving the long side a material edge despite a bearish FII outflow of ₹930.9 Cr.

bear.thesis_summary: The trade fails because the "oversold" RSI 26.62 is not a mean-reversion signal in a downtrend — it is a trend-strength signal. With MACD bearish, price below the 200DMA, and FIIs selling ₹930.9 Cr over 30 days, the stock is in a structural downtrend where RSI can remain oversold (or drop further) for weeks while price grinds lower. The bull thesis assumes a "bounce" is the default path; the data shows a "continuation" is the path of least resistance. The neutral PCR 0.998 does not imply support — it implies options market indifference, which in a downtrend means no put protection buying (no fear) and no call selling (no supply overhead), just apathy. In a LOW_VOL regime (VIX 12.81, HV Rank 9.7), oversold bounces are shallow and short-lived because realized vol compresses the rebound magnitude. The 0.7% friction cost is not "modest" when the expected bounce in a 9.7 percentile vol environment is measured in single-digit rupees against an ATR of ₹60.66 — the trade pays spread and slippage for a move that statistically fails to exceed noise.
